name: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
publisher: OWASP GenAI Security Project (Independent Academic Reference)
disclaimer: This is an independent academic implementation inspired by the mapping concept of the OWASP GenAI Security Project Crosswalk. No official OWASP affiliation, endorsement, or certification is claimed.

controls.title: Prompt Injection
controls.description: Manipulating LLM behavior through crafted user inputs directly concatenated into prompts or indirect injection via external untrusted data sources (web, documents, emails).
controls.verification_guidance: Check for parameterized prompts, system-user prompt isolation, input validation, guardrail classifiers, and separation of external untrusted content.

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.description: LLM outputs or logs revealing proprietary algorithms, PII, intellectual property, credentials, or internal system configurations to unauthorized users.
controls.verification_guidance: Check for output scrubbing/redaction, strict access controls on context data, DLP scanning on prompts/responses, and absence of hardcoded API keys/secrets.

controls.title: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
controls.description: Risks from third-party pre-trained models, vulnerable plugins, third-party datasets, tampered model weights, or vulnerable AI SDK dependencies.
controls.verification_guidance: Verify cryptographic hashes on model weights, use of trusted registries, software bill of materials (SBOM), safe serialization formats (safetensors instead of pickle), and pinned dependencies.

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.description: Manipulation of training data or fine-tuning datasets to introduce backdoors, biases, vulnerabilities, or ethical bypasses into the model.
controls.verification_guidance: Check training dataset integrity, anomaly detection on ingested RAG data, data provenance tracking, and role-based training pipelines.

controls.title: Insecure Output Handling
controls.description: Neglecting to validate or sanitize LLM outputs before feeding them into downstream components (e.g., eval(), SQL queries, system shells, or innerHTML).
controls.verification_guidance: Verify that downstream sinks treat LLM output as untrusted user input, employing parameterized queries, strict schema validation, escaping, and prohibiting direct exec/eval.

controls.title: Excessive Agency
controls.description: Granting autonomous LLM agents excessive privileges, unrestricted tool access, or high-impact actions (file deletion, network writes, money transfer) without human-in-the-loop authorization.
controls.verification_guidance: Examine tool permissions, read-only vs write scoping, human-in-the-loop confirmations for state-changing operations, and rate/action limiting.

controls.title: System Prompt Leakage
controls.description: Extraction of internal system instructions, secret rules, API parameters, or behavioral constraints through adversarial prompting.
controls.verification_guidance: Ensure sensitive business logic, keys, or internal endpoints are not stored inside system prompt strings; implement prompt leakage detection filters.

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.description: Vulnerabilities in RAG systems where attackers poison embeddings, manipulate similarity search, or bypass vector database access controls.
controls.verification_guidance: Audit vector database multitenancy, document authorization metadata checking at retrieval time, query input sanitization, and embedding collision resilience.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.description: LLM generating factually incorrect, fabricated, or misleading outputs (hallucinations) presented as authoritative facts without verification.
controls.verification_guidance: Check for citation anchoring, source verification, temperature settings, deterministic guardrails, and user disclaimer notifications.

controls.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls.description: Denial of service or resource exhaustion caused by excessive token processing, looping agent calls, expensive embeddings, or large context windows without rate limits.
controls.verification_guidance: Check max_tokens limits, per-user rate limiting, agent recursion limits (max_iterations), request timeouts, and token budget alerts.
